text:
Cole Hutson was a second-round pick in 2024, and second-round defensemen are not supposed to look like this at 20. He has nine points in 15 games, including a two-goal night against Nashville that RMNB headlined with his own shrug: "Lucky it went in." Spencer Carbery has explained to RMNB why Hutson is thriving next to Jack St. Ivany and how Washington is managing his minutes, which are a steady 19 a night.

For context, defensemen picked in his range since 2005 scored a median 0.21 points a game in their first real season; he is at 0.60. Some of that will cool. He is shooting about 14%, double a typical defenseman, and his teammates are finishing a little above their chances with him on. But the base is solid: the Capitals get the better of the 5v5 chances with him out there (53.7%), he skates and shoots in the top fifth of the league, and he gets to dangerous ice for a defenseman. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has only four of his games so far, too few to say much. Our projection is about 47 points, with a wide range.
headline: Cole Hutson is ahead of every schedule
